items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to requirements for licensure
of certain mental health practitioners and providing certain mental health
practitioners authority to give diagnosis
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4463

SPONSOR: HELMING
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to requirements for
licensure of certain mental health practitioners and providing certain
mental health practitioners authority to give diagnosis

 
PURPOSE:

To establish a pathway for current and future licensed mental health
counselors, marriage and family therapists, and licensed psychoanalysts
to diagnose by amending the requirements for licensure and developing a
diagnosis privilege for those currently licensed who have satisfied
certain requirements.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends Section 8401 of the education law to establish a defi-
nition for the term "diagnosis" for both licensed mental health counse-
lors (LMHCs), marriage and family therapists, and licensed psycho-ana-
lysts (LPs).

Section 2: Amends Section 8402 of the education law, to change the scope
of practice of licensed mental health counselors to include the authori-
ty to diagnose after satisfying certain requirements.

Section 3: Amends Section 8402 of the education law to specify that the
education required for a license as a mental health counselor must
include 12 credit hours of clinical courses and that 2,000 of the 3,000
hours required for supervised experience be direct client contact hours.

Section 4: Creates a new section 8402-A to establish a diagnosis privi-
lege when certain requirements are satisfied by either existing LMHCs or
new applicants.

Section 5: Amends Section 8403 of the education la to change the scope
of practice of licensed marriage and family therapists to include the
authority to diagnose after satisfying certain requirements.

Section 6: Amends Section 8402 of the education law to specify that the
education required for a license as a marriage and family therapist must
include 12 credit hours of clinical courses and that 2,000 of the 3,000
hours required for the supervised experience be direct client contact
hours.

Section 7: Creates a new Section 8403-A to establish a diagnosis privi-
lege when certain requirements are satisfied by either existing MFTs or
new applicants.

Section 8: Amends Section 8405 of the education law to change the scope
of practice of licensed psychoanalysts to include the authority to diag-
nose after satisfying certain requirements.

Section 9: Amends Section 8405 of the education law to specify that the
education required for a license as a psychoanalyst must include 12
credit hours of clinical courses and the 2,000 hours required for super-
vised experience be direct client contact hours.
Section 10: Creates a new section 8405-A to establish a diagnosis privi-
lege when certain requirements are satisfied by either existing LPs or
new applicants.

Section 11: Amends Section 8409 of the education law to allow for more
time under a limited permit for both mental health counselor and
psycho-analyst applicants to gain specific experience under supervision.

Section 12: Amends Section 8410 to ensure that currently employed LPs
and LMHCs are allowed to continue the current activities set forth in
their employment when the state and municipal exemption expires.

Section 13: Creates a new section 8412-A to require, that any continuing
education courses used to satisfy the requirements for diagnosis privi-
lege be separately reviewed and approved by NYSED.

Section 14: Sets forth the effective dates.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Chapter 676 of the Laws of 2002 provided for the license of mental
health counselors, marriage and family therapists, and licensed psycho-
analysts. These psychotherapy professionals have the authority to "use
assessment instruments and mental health counseling and psychotherapy to
identify, evaluate, and treat dysfunctions and disorders." However, none
of these professions were given the authority to diagnose.

Modeling the licensure requirements for newly licensed mental health
counselors, marriage and family therapists, and psychoanalysts to the
licensure requirements of licensed clinical social workers who currently
have the authority to diagnose will provide New Yorkers confidence that
these licensed professionals are competent to diagnose. In addition,
advancing pathways for current licensed mental health counselors,
marriage and family therapists, and licensed psychoanalysts to achieve a
diagnosis privilege will further ensure competency.

Establishing the ability to have diagnosis privilege will enable these
highly qualified psychotherapy professionals to provide a full array of
services for those seeking mental health services. As the need for
comprehensive mental health services increases within the State's
vulnerable populations - adolescents, veterans, and the elderly -
providing a pathway to diagnosis privilege for licensed mental health
counselors, marriage and family therapists, and licensed psychoanalysts
will increase access across the state.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2021-2022: S.3221 referred to Higher Education/A.5751 referred to Higher
Education

2020: A.4383-A amended and recommit to Higher Education

2019: A.4383 referred to Higher Education

2018: S.6582-A/ A8757-A amended and recommit to Higher Education

2017: 5.6582 referred to Rules/A.8757 referred to Higher Education

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Professional fees would offset any fiscal impact on the New York State
Education Department

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect one year after it shall become law, provided
that sections four, seven, and ten shall take effect on January 1, 2026,
provided further that effective immediately, the state education depart-
ment may make any rules or regulations as deemed necessary to implement
the act.

summary: Relates to requirements for licensure of mental health counselors and marriage and family therapists and providing mental health counselors and marriage and family therapists authority to give diagnosis.
